title: Macbeth, Full Summary in Verse
author: Mr Salles Teaches English
summary: This piece is a full rhyming-couplet retelling of Macbeth built explicitly as a memory aid, packaged with a set of literary interpretations the author argues most students never actually encounter in school — for example, that Macbeth's psychological need for his wife to manipulate him is itself a character trait, that the belly-unzipping of Macdonwald at the play's opening mirrors Macduff's own caesarean birth at the close, and that Lady Macbeth's suicide is driven less by guilt over Duncan's murder than by guilt at having unleashed her husband as a psychopath rather than a warrior. Alongside the pedagogical content, the piece is candid about its own AI-animation production process: dozens of individually scripted and prompted 8-10 second clips assembled into a 13-minute video, explicitly framed as still requiring real effort and creative judgment rather than being a shortcut. The verse itself functions as the actual teaching tool — compressing plot, character motivation, and thematic argument (Lady Macbeth as an Eve/Original Sin figure, the Porter's dual comedic purposes) into memorable rhymed lines meant to stick with students preparing for exams. Its underlying pedagogical claim is that literary analysis doesn't have to be delivered as prose exposition to carry real interpretive weight — a rhyming summary can smuggle in genuine, non-obvious critical readings while being far easier for students to retain.
points: Packages non-obvious literary interpretations into a memorable, rhymed-verse format: that Macbeth psychologically depends on his wife's manipulation rather than being merely a victim of it.
Draws an interpretive parallel most students never encounter: Macbeth 'unzipping' Macdonwald's belly at the play's start mirrors Macduff's own caesarean birth ('untimely ripp'd') at the end.
Reframes Lady Macbeth's suicide motive: not guilt over Duncan's murder itself, but guilt at having unleashed her husband as a psychopath instead of a warrior.
Documents the actual labor behind the AI-animated video (roughly 78 individually scripted and prompted clips for 13 minutes) as a counterargument to 'AI is just cheating.'
quotes: It includes key quotes and crucial interpretations — ideas that you probably have not been taught in school. For example: Macbeth knows his wife will try to manipulate him, and actually depends on this.

There is an ironic symmetry between Macbeth unzipping Macdonwald's belly at the beginning, and at the end meeting Macduff who unzipped his mother's belly to be born - untimely ripp'd. The image and metaphor come full circle.
Lady Macbeth doesn't kill herself because of guilt at killing Duncan, but because of the guilt she feels in unleashing her husband as a psycopath instead of a warrior.

It's a 13 minute video, which means a minimum of 78 clips, each of which I had to script, write a prompt, and wait for the generation... So, sure, AI is cheating, but it still feels a lot like effort and work!
Learn from this tale of brave Macbeth / Who gave the Vikings gruesome death. / A warrior with a bloodstained hand, / The fiercest fighter in the land.
